bib.title: Solving Challenging Math Word Problems Using GPT-4 Code Interpreter with Code-based Self-Verification

read.skipped: Figures 7 and 8 (MMLU per-subject charts) are image-only; only labels extracted. Reference list skimmed.

question: Can GPT-4 Code Interpreter be prompted to verify and correct its own math answers with code, and can the verification state improve majority voting?
hypothesis: More frequent code use, including code that checks the answer, raises accuracy; verified-True answers are more reliable and deserve more voting weight.
contributions: First systematic analysis of the role of code generation, execution and self-debugging in GPT4-Code's math solving.
Explicit code-based self-verification (CSV) prompt and verification-guided weighted majority voting.
Two new instruction-following datasets, MATH-code and MMLU-Math-code (stated as released or to be released).

method.summary: Zero-shot prompts constrain how GPT-4 Code Interpreter uses code (none, once, unrestricted) to measure Code Usage Frequency against accuracy. The CSV prompt asks the model to verify its answer with code and revise if the check is False; k sampled solutions are then voted with weights by verification state (True, Uncertain, False).
method.task: math word problem solving (MATH, GSM8K, MMLU-Math, MMLU-STEM)

datasets.name: MATH
datasets.split: inferred: test set, seven subjects, five difficulty levels; size not stated

models.name: GPT-4 Code Interpreter (GPT4-Code)
models.architecture: GPT-4 with incremental code generation and execution

inference.decoding: inferred: sampling of k independent paths for voting; decoding settings not stated
inference.samples: k=16 sampled paths for MATH voting; 5 for GSM8K; single run otherwise; seeds and repeat runs not stated; MMLU voting k not stated
inference.prompting: zero-shot, no few-shot examples; code-use constraint prompts and the CSV prompt

parameters.voting_weights: wT=1, wU=0.5, wF=0.2 (wT > wU > wF); main setting
parameters.voting_score: Score(a) = sum over paths with answer a of w_v, v in {True, Uncertain, False}; output argmax_a Score(a)

other.code_usage_frequency: number of code executions per solution, measured for each prompt
other.false_state_note: once an answer is confirmed False, no further verification may be run, giving a False state

metrics.name: Accuracy
metrics.definition: share of problems with a correct final answer

metrics.name: Code Usage Frequency
metrics.definition: number of code executions per solution under a prompt

metrics.name: Precision of verification
metrics.definition: TP/(TP+FP); share of verified-True answers that were correct

metrics.name: Recall of verification
metrics.definition: TP/(TP+FN); share of correct answers verified True

eval.protocol: Single run per configuration as far as stated; no significance tests or confidence intervals; precision and recall computed from five sampled paths.

availability.data: MATH-code and MMLU-Math-code experimental data said to be public ('making ... publicly available'; later 'will make it publicly available in the near future'); no URL

prompts.text: You are not allowed to use any code. The problem is: {Question}.
You can use code only 1 time. The problem is: {Question}.
Solve the problem and put your answer in \boxed{}. The problem is: {Question}.
To solve the problem using code interpreter step by step, and please verify your answer using code interpreter.

results.claim: CSV alone lifts GPT4-Code on MATH from 69.69% to 73.54%.
results.setup: MATH, GPT4-Code, zero-shot, single path, overall across 7 subjects
results.quote: raising the result to 73.54% after adding explicit code-based self-verification

results.claim: CSV plus verification-guided weighted voting with 16 paths reaches 84.32% on MATH.
results.setup: MATH, GPT4-Code, k=16 sampled paths, wT=1, wU=0.5, wF=0.2
results.quote: 84.32% after adding both explicit code-based self-verification and verification-guided weighted majority voting (the number of sampled paths is 16)
results.note: Abstract writes 53.9% to 84.3%, comparing with the previous state of the art, not with GPT4-Code.

results.claim: Basic GPT4-Code scores 69.69% on MATH, against 42.20% for GPT-4 and 53.90% for GPT-4 PHP.
results.setup: MATH, zero-shot; GPT-4 (PHP) figure is from Zheng et al. 2023
results.note: Intro rounds to 69.7% and says 27.5% over GPT-4 (42.2%).

results.claim: Natural-language self-verification does not help: 69.29% versus 69.69% without verification, and 4 of 7 subjects decline.
results.setup: MATH, GPT4-Code, NL verification prompt instead of code
results.quote: relying solely on natural language verification
results.table: Table 4, row Nature Language, column Overall
results.note: Table 4 lists Number Theory change as +8.4 for code-based while Table 1 lists +7.6; 85.6-77.2 = 8.4.

results.setup: MATH, five sampled paths, True state counted as positive

results.claim: Allowing code once raises accuracy 6.9 points over no code.
results.quote: Prompt 2 yields an accuracy gain of 6.9 percent over Prompt

results.claim: On GSM8K, CSV plus voting with 5 paths reaches 97.0%, against 92.9% for GPT4-Code and 96.5% for PHP with 40 paths.
results.table: Table 2, row GPT4-Code + CSV + Voting, column Accuracy(%)

results.claim: On MMLU-Math, CSV plus voting gives 89.2% against 87.5% for GPT4-Code, both zero-shot.
results.setup: MMLU-Math, zero-shot, GPT4-Code; k not stated
results.table: Table 3, row GPT4-Code + CSV + Voting, dataset Math

results.claim: On MMLU-STEM, CSV plus voting gives 87.0% against 86.8% for GPT4-Code.
results.table: Table 3, row GPT4-Code + CSV + Voting, dataset STEM

results.claim: Geometry gains only 0.6 points from CSV, which the authors tie to multimodality.
results.quote: the Geometry problem only has an increased accuracy of 0.6%

results.claim: Weights satisfying wT > wU >= wF beat naive voting at every path count; weights 0.5/0.5/1 do worse than naive voting.
results.setup: MATH, k=2..16 paths, Fig 6(b); numbers only in figure
results.quote: the performance of the verification-guided weighted majority voting consistently surpassed that of the naive majority voting methods across all sampled paths

limits: Only GPT-4 Code Interpreter is studied; authors concede this and plan other LLMs.
Closed model accessed through ChatGPT; version, date, temperature and sampling settings not reported, so exact rerun is not possible.
MATH test size, number of runs and variance are not given; no significance tests.
Verification can be Uncertain or skipped after False; recall is only 79.11%, so many correct answers are not verified True.
Code Usage Frequency correlation with accuracy is observational across prompts; CSV also changes the prompt wording.
Weights were chosen and ablated on the same MATH set; voting weight ablation values are only in Fig 6(b).
Evaluated 2023 model; the 69.69% baseline is now dated.
Data release is promised but no URL given.
